central_replacement.principle: One live ordered HTTP stack with explicit Route identities; one retained legacy routing.Router for WebSocket resolution/profile. Do not route HTTP through global specificity selection or unwrap one preselected RouteChain.

classes.name: internal.HttpRouter
classes.signature: final class HttpRouter { synchronized HttpRoute appendRoute(PathSpec path); synchronized void appendUse(PathSpec prefix, Middleware callback); synchronized void appendError(PathSpec prefix, ErrorMiddleware callback); synchronized void appendMount(PathSpec prefix, HttpRouter child); HttpLayer[] snapshot(); }
classes.ownership: Stores ordered layers and param callback registrations; volatile published immutable layer-array snapshots for safe late registration. No dependency types.

classes.name: internal.HttpLayer
classes.signature: final class HttpLayer { enum Kind { USE, ROUTE, ERROR, MOUNT } final Kind kind; final PathSpec matcher; final Object payload; }
classes.ownership: Holds FULL route or PREFIX use/mount compiled matcher. Matching raw captures+matchedPath from HttpPathPattern feed a separate UTF8-decoding utility.

classes.name: internal.HttpRoute
classes.signature: final class HttpRoute { final long identity; final PathSpec path; synchronized void append(String methodToken, HttpCallback callback); HttpRouteHandler[] snapshot(); boolean handles(String methodToken); }
classes.ownership: One app.route(path) call appends exactly one route layer immediately, even before handlers are attached. Builder method calls mutate that Route; separate app.get calls append distinct Route identities.

classes.name: internal.RequestExecution
classes.signature: final class RequestExecution { void start(); void resume(Frame frame, Signal signal); void responseDone(); void callbackEnter(); void callbackExit(); void abort(Throwable cause); }
classes.ownership: Owns one Request/Response, router+route frames/cursors, current error mode, Router-local param caches, OPTIONS accumulation and completion/cleanup state. Handles synchronous reentry and queued cross-thread continuations.

classes.name: internal.RouterFrame
classes.signature: final class RouterFrame { final HttpRouter router; final RouterFrame parent; final RequestView savedMountView; int layerIndex; RouteFrame route; Map<String,ParamResult> paramCache; }
classes.ownership: Scope param cache per Router invocation; saved view restored at mount exit. Child mergeParams merges parent/child with child values taking precedence. Do not restore all params after every ordinary next.run return.

classes.name: internal.RouteFrame
classes.signature: final class RouteFrame { final HttpRoute route; int handlerIndex; final String effectiveMethodToken; }
classes.ownership: Route-local method iteration and HEAD fallback. next.route skips remaining callbacks of current identity; next.router exits current Router frame.

classes.name: internal.RequestView
classes.signature: final class RequestView { final String path; final String url; final String baseUrl; final Map<String,List<String>> params; }
classes.ownership: Immutable current layer view, published on the same DefaultRequest instance. Original exchange, body/cache/attributes/uploads/requestId/application remain request-global.

central_replacement.path_spec: Use a focused PathSpec interface for compile-once FULL/PREFIX matching and alternatives. String uses HttpPathPattern; Java Pattern uses Java semantics/own flags and per-match Matcher. Do not overload a single legacy RoutePattern to serve both new HTTP and old WS contracts.
central_replacement.publication_and_late_registration: Use synchronized append+volatile array publication for router layers and Route handlers. HTTP registration/use/route-builder attachments after listen are allowed while app is live; retain configuration-only guards for server options, codecs, WS profile and shutdown as expressly scoped. Current request cursor snapshot policy must be tested against the fixed oracle; a fresh snapshot on continuation can observe newly appended layers, while a permanent request-start snapshot can differ. Do not assume snapshot-at-request-start is fully equivalent without that test.

Request: Keep String param(String name) as existing NaruServe convenience: first scalar/list element; missing/absent throws IllegalArgumentException (unless SRS explicitly chooses a nullable migration).
Add @Nullable String paramOrNull(String name): absent optional or undeclared -> null; empty participating capture -> empty string.
Add List<String> paramValues(String name): immutable singleton for scalar, full list for wildcard, empty list for absent; never conflate wildcard list with a slash-joined scalar.
Add Map<String,List<String>> pathParams(): immutable present values only; optional nonparticipants omitted; duplicate capture names follow last binding from compiler/oracle.
String path(): current mount-relative RAW pathname, matching Express req.path; do not percent-decode entire request pathname during Request construction.
String url(): current mount-relative raw path plus original raw query when present, preserving an empty trailing question mark.
String baseUrl(): actual consumed mount text, with original percent-encoding and case; String originalUrl(): immutable original raw path+query.

Keep rawPath() as the original exchange raw pathname for NaruServe compatibility and logging/upgrade; route execution uses RequestView.path, not rawPath(). If choosing current rawPath instead, explicitly revise old contract/tests and provide original-path accessor.
Optional decodedPath() convenience may preserve former whole-path decoded view, but is never used for matching/routing/security identity. It is not required to implement Express matching.
DefaultRequest.applyView(RequestView) package-private; originalUrl/originalRawPath initialized once; do not reconstruct request per layer.
public_api_recommendation.decode_boundary: Match raw pathname first. Decode participating capture bytes once with strictUTF8; invalid escape/UTF8 in a matched capture is400. A malformed percent sequence outside a capture must not be globally rejected merely by constructing DefaultRequest; exact literal cases follow oracle/transport boundary. Static filesystem safety remains separate at file access.
Next: Retain void run() and void error(Throwable).
Add void route() and void router() (unambiguous Java names); use-only next.route behaves like normal continuation.
Default methods for new Next operations may preserve old binary implementations if necessary, but actual common HTTP ChainNext overrides them.
Remove universal consumed/owner-thread/response-completed bans from new HTTP Next. Repeated explicit next and explicit next after response completion still drive callbacks according to oracle.
RouteHandler existing2-arg remains terminal-style Java convenience; add Middleware3-arg route overloads/varargs for callbacks that can continue and preserve existing2-arg lambdas/method references.
Router: Add public com.snoworca.naruserve.Router.create() and Router.create(boolean mergeParams) delegating to internal.HttpRouter. Keep old com.snoworca.naruserve.routing.Router separate as legacy resolver.
RestApp.use(String prefix, Router child), use(Router child); Router provides corresponding route/use/param methods without application lifecycle/server config.
Avoid duplicating registry/matcher execution: both DefaultRestApp and public Router delegate to focused HttpRouter/registration support.

Add explicit param hook registration. Recommended ParamHandler.handle(Request req, Response res, Next next, List<String> value, String name) to retain wildcard list semantics and scalar singleton; API names/overloads need Java/Kotlin compilation tests.
errors: Add @FunctionalInterface ErrorMiddleware.handle(Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next).

Add use(ErrorMiddleware) and use(String prefix, ErrorMiddleware): lambda arity4 distinguishes existing Middleware3-arg. In error mode skip normal callbacks; error-next.run clears error; error-next.error replaces current error; thrown exceptions enter same ordered cursor.

Preserve onError(ErrorHandler3-arg) as a documented NaruServe extension bridge. A wrapper can invoke it at its registered stack position and, if still NEW, continue the current error automatically to preserve old terminal-hook behavior. Do not silently treat its missing Next as the full Express error-middleware API.

Keep StandardErrors JSON utilities/configuration as extension. New common finalhandler/404/errors need a separate FinalHandler boundary and oracle-defined status/essential headers/body; do not retain blanket405/501/defaultJSON as common behavior without SRS decision.
async: No mandatory CompletionStage/CompletableFuture (AndroidAPI24) and no new library.
Deferred next via captured Next works independently of promise-like API.

If representing returned async rejection is required, add an own Java8/API21 Deferred/AsyncResult with own functional failure callback, resolve(), reject(Throwable) and subscription; attach rejection to the current execution cursor, resolve without response/next does nothing.
Prefer explicitly named getAsync/useAsync or an explicit adapter over overloaded same-arity return-valued lambdas that may break existing Java RouteHandler overload resolution.
Do not require java.util.function.Consumer in the mandatory API21 surface; own functional callback interface avoids another API24 compatibility trap.

execution_and_lifetime.continuations: Same-thread reentrant next.run executes downstream synchronously so after-next observations remain correct. A different thread enqueues a signal and returns if another callback owns the execution; when no callback owns it, the caller may take execution ownership. Never hold a request-wide blocking lock across user code: a handler can start another thread calling next and join it; blocking that thread on the original callback would deadlock.
execution_and_lifetime.serialization: Short state lock protects cursor/queue/owner transitions; user callbacks and transport IO outside that lock. Reentrant same-owner recursion allowed. Queued cross-thread signals drain when current callback unwinds. Define/test the Java cross-thread enqueue behavior explicitly; Express has no simultaneous JS callback threads.
execution_and_lifetime.no_auto_finish: Initial handler return or fulfilled Deferred does not finish a NEW response and does not auto-next. Only stack exhaustion invokes final404/OPTIONS/error handler; response send/end, abort or timeout terminates transport.
execution_and_lifetime.response_hook: DefaultResponse.onDone currently holds ONE replaceable Runnable; register one RequestExecution-owned callback composing log + terminal status + cleanup trigger, rather than adding competing callbacks.
split_afterHandler: Replace common HTTP afterHandler NEW->empty200 with callbackReturned(): sets handlerDone and starts an already pending stream transfer, never implicitly commits NEW.
Keep existing DefaultResponse stream(in) late-start branch: when handlerDone=true the caller runs transfer itself; this is useful for deferred text/stream completion.
After each callback exit, run pending transfer only when its handler unwound; retain afterFailure/abort transport ownership. Legacy WS path can keep its legacy completion policy where required.
execution_and_lifetime.cleanup: Track response terminal flag, active user callback count, queued/executing signals and cleanup-once flag. Release uploads exactly once only after terminal response and current callbacks/queue drain, so save(upload) after res.send within the same callback remains valid. Pending deferred request keeps uploads/body/services. Initial Dispatcher finally does not alone prove chain end. Late explicit next after terminal is not globally banned; resource access after terminal cleanup follows documented lifecycle and never writes another response.
execution_and_lifetime.logging: Exactly one access line at terminal completion/abort using immutable original method/path/requestId/start. Preserve dedicated SSE cause/duration lines and WS101/session logging. Do not log every resumed callback.
execution_and_lifetime.application_context: GatedExchangeHandler currently marks AppLifecycle.requestThread only around initial Dispatcher.handle. Add a scoped withRequest(Runnable) that remembers prior ThreadLocal value and restores it; every later callback/drain that may call shutdown uses that scope. Plain enter/remove is insufficient for nested request reentry.
execution_and_lifetime.shutdown: Keep start gate and configuration lifecycle unchanged except scoped HTTP registration guard. Register open RequestExecutions in an app registry before dispatch; terminal cleanup unregisters. Shutdown refuses new requests, waits/graces active executions, then aborts pending transports and closes owned resources once. The adapter-specific registry/finish callbacks integrate with this; do not conflate SSE counts with ordinary deferred requests.

param_hooks.cache_key: Router invocation frame, param name -> last matched value plus transformed value/error/skip result; not a permanent request(name,value) set. Parent and child same name/value execute separately.
param_hooks.ordering: Route matching assigns current capture view, then registered hooks run in token/parameter order before callbacks. Duplicate params lastwins, absent optional absent. Hook can mutate current params or route/error signal; cache replays corresponding result for same last value.
param_hooks.restoration: Mount boundary restores saved url/baseUrl/parent view. Do not unconditionally pop params after every same-Router next call; after-next may observe downstream route params according to existing oracle.

method_and_defaults.must_change: Dispatcher.preCheck currently rejects unknown enum methods and path validator before matching, and HTTP fallback maps METHOD_MISMATCH to405. Common ordered HTTP path must not retain those gates globally.
method_and_defaults.method_model: Need common method-token registration (including Node-supported verbs beyond current9) and Request.methodToken(); preserve existing Method enum convenience, expand/model additional common tokens explicitly. Do not map unfamiliar methods toGET. Java enum name for M-SEARCH requires an explicit token mapping.
method_and_defaults.head: HEAD fallback is per Route: use its explicit HEAD callbacks if present, otherwise that Route's GET callbacks, respecting route order. No global later-HEAD preference.
method_and_defaults.options: Accumulate methods for matching route layers that are traversed, addHEAD forGET, dedup and alphabetical comma+space sort. Send OPTIONS only after actual stack fallthrough; downstream middleware may answer first. OPTIONS* remains transport-specific existing contract unless changed explicitly.
method_and_defaults.static: Preserve static convenience as an explicitly ordered/labeled extension bridge. Existing statics fallback checks only terminal no-match/mismatch; do not let it preempt user downstream middleware, root traversal guards or ordered common routes.

compatibility_bridges: Keep legacy Router/RoutePattern/RouterPolicy strict defaults for WS profile; route matcher worker HttpPathPattern is HTTP-only.

Preserve Dispatcher(Router<RouteHandler>) and internal constructor shapes for legacy low-level tests initially through a legacy adapter mode, while DefaultRestApp uses the new HTTP stack path. Do not let that bridge hide missing common app behavior.

Preserve MiddlewarePipeline/ChainNext as legacy WS middleware if needed; new HTTP Next implementation delegates to RequestExecution. Reusing old class names is optional, reusing old bans is incorrect.
DefaultRouteGroup delegates into unified registration; route-local group middleware becomes callbacks in one Route, not a detached global prefix pipeline.
DefaultRouteBuilder holds an HttpRoute identity rather than snapshotting a middleware list into every independently registered handler.

known_old_tests_requiring_contract_cited.conflict: Old one-use/same-thread/after-response/initial-return expiry assumptions contradict new common HTTP continuation behavior. Replace only after SRS update; add oracle-cited repeated/post-response/deferred tests, preserve extension-specific lifecycle evidence.
NEW autoempty200 after callback return contradicts pending async/no-next semantics.
Common mismatch404, new string grammar and ordered duplicate routes differ; WS/legacy matcher cases remain protected.
Assertions probing freeze by attempting app.get must change to a configuration-only guard probe; startup gate/config freeze still applies while common HTTP late registration is allowed.

Some tests assert global onError auto-chain, JSON fallback, dropped second error and synchronous exception propagation. Retain documented onError extension semantics but add ordered ErrorMiddleware/cleared/replaced/rejected error cases; do not treat old extension tests as Express finalhandler proof.

test_requirements: registration interleaving and route identity before handler attachment
late app registration and late Route-builder attachment
repeatednext/postresponse-next and cross-thread join deadlock regression
deferred success/no-next pending and rejection-to-error, including initially rejected async results
mount prefix actual text/url/baseUrl restoration and mergeParams
Router-local param cache transformed values/error/skip/last-value behavior
HEAD per-route and OPTIONS downstream intercept/final alphabetic list
request identity/bodycache/upload save after send and terminal cleanup exactlyonce
shutdown called inside resumed callback with lifecycle scope
implementation_order: First central coherent HTTP request/registration/execution slice with current helper contracts; mount+param+error+async features extend those same cursor objects. Then parallel adapters/extensions. Do not implement a second dispatcher per issue or split shared DefaultRestApp/Dispatcher/RequestExecution writes across concurrent workers.
